item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABPZ20 KNHC 111138
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
500 AM PDT Sun Oct 11 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Post-Tropical
Cyclone Rachel, located inland over southern California and on
Hurricane Simon, located just offshore of southwestern Mexico.

South of Southern Mexico:
A tropical wave over the far eastern East Pacific is producing
disorganized showers and thunderstorms. Environmental conditions are
expected to be conducive for gradual development, and a tropical
depression is likely to form well south of southern Mexico by the
middle or latter half of the week as the system moves generally
west-northwestward at around 10 mph.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...20 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...80 percent.

$$
Forecaster Kelly
item.author: nhcwebmaster@noaa.gov (NHC Webmaster)

item.title: Post-Tropical Cyclone Rachel Public Advisory Number 57a
item.description:
Issued at 500 AM PDT Sun Oct 11 2026 
000
WTPZ33 KNHC 111140
TCPEP3
 
BULLETIN
Post-Tropical Cyclone Rachel Intermediate Advisory Number 57A
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP182026
500 AM PDT Sun Oct 11 2026
 
...RACHEL CONTINUES TO BRING HEAVY RAINS AND GUSTY WINDS TO
PORTIONS OF BAJA CALIFORNIA AND THE SOUTHWESTERN UNITED STATES...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 500 AM PDT...1200 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...33.9N 115.4W
ABOUT 270 MI...435 KM N OF PUNTA BAJA MEXICO
ABOUT 130 MI...205 KM NE OF SAN DIEGO CALIFORNIA
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...40 MPH...65 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...N OR 10 DEGREES AT 25 MPH...41 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...993 MB...29.33 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
CHANGES WITH THIS ADVISORY:
 
The government of Mexico has discontinued the Tropical Storm Warning 
for the west coast of Baja California and Baja California Sur, from 
Punta Eugenia northward to the U.S./Mexico Border, and the Tropical 
Storm Watch for the east coast of Baja California, from Bahia De Los 
Angeles northward to Isla San Luis and northwest Mexico from Puerto 
Libertad to Puerto Penasco.
 
SUMMARY OF WATCHES AND WARNINGS IN EFFECT:
 
A Tropical Storm Warning is in effect for...
* East coast of Baja California, from Isla San Luis northward to
Puerto Penasco
 
A Tropical Storm Warning means that tropical storm conditions are
expected somewhere within the warning area.

For storm information specific to your area in the United States, 
please monitor products issued by your local National Weather 
Service forecast office. For storm information specific to your area 
outside of the United States, please monitor products issued by your 
national meteorological service.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 500 AM PDT (1200 UTC), the center of Post-Tropical Cyclone Rachel 
was located near latitude 33.9 North, longitude 115.4 West. The 
post-tropical cyclone is moving toward the north near 25 mph     
(41 km/h) and this motion is expected to continue today as Rachel 
moves farther inland over the southwest United States.
 
Maximum sustained winds have decreased to near 40 mph (65 km/h) with 
higher gusts. Rachel should continue to weaken and dissipate later 
today.
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 160 miles (260 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 993 mb (29.33 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
Key messages for Rachel can be found in the Tropical Cyclone
Discussion under AWIPS header MIATCDEP3 and WMO header WTPZ43 KNHC.
 
WIND: Tropical storm conditions are occuring over portions of the 
Baja California Peninsula within the Tropical Storm Warning area, 
and these conditions will continue for the next few hours. Strong 
gusty winds associated with the system are spreading over interior 
portions of the southwestern United States, especially in areas of 
higher terrain, today and tomorrow.
 
RAINFALL: Rachel will bring 1 to 2 inches of rain to portions of
northern Baja California this weekend.
 
Rachel and its associated moisture will also bring rainfall of 1 to 
3 inches, with maximum amounts locally up to 5 inches from Southern 
California into the Great Basin and portions of the southwestern 
United States this weekend. This will lead to increasing coverage of 
rainfall and potential for significant flash and urban flooding.
 
For a complete depiction of forecast rainfall associated with
Rachel, please see the National Weather Service Storm Total Rainfall
Graphic available at
hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep3.shtml?rainqpf and the Flash Flood Risk
graphic at hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep3.shtml?ero.
 
SURF: Waves generated by Rachel will continue along the coasts of 
Southern California and northern Baja California today. These waves, 
combined with an incoming long-period southerly swell, will cause 
life-threatening surf and rip current conditions. Coastal flooding 
and erosion are expected to worsen this morning as the highest waves 
coincide with the high tides and water levels that are already 
running well above predicted levels. Moderate to major coastal 
flooding is expected, with hazardous coastal conditions continuing 
into early next week. Please consult products from your local 
weather office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 800 AM PDT.
 
$$
Forecaster Kelly
item.author: nhcwebmaster@noaa.gov (NHC Webmaster)

item.title: Post-Tropical Cyclone Rachel Forecast Discussion Number 57
item.description:
Issued at 200 AM PDT Sun Oct 11 2026 
000
WTPZ43 KNHC 110857
TCDEP3
 
Post-Tropical Cyclone Rachel Discussion Number  57
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP182026
200 AM PDT Sun Oct 11 2026

The bulk of the heavy rainfall is generally on the northern side of 
Rachel, consistent with extratropical transition, as it continues to 
move farther inland. The current intensity of 45 kt is based on a 
blend of a recent ASCAT pass and guidance from the global models, 
with the strongest winds located well to the southeast over the 
northern Gulf of California. 

The initial motion is estimated to be northward, or 010/22 kt, and 
the system is expected to accelerate as it moves farther inland. 
The current NHC track was slightly adjusted westward based on the 
global models. Rachel is expected to steadily weaken over land
during the day and dissipate by tonight. However, the remnants of 
Rachel will continue to produce heavy rainfall and gusty winds over 
parts of the southwestern United States and northwestern Mexico. 
See products issued by the Weather Prediction Center and local 
National Weather Service offices for more information. 
 
Key Messages:
 
1. Tropical storm conditions are expected in portions of northern 
Baja California and portions of northwestern Mexico, where Tropical 
Storm Warnings are in effect. Tropical storm conditions are also 
possible in eastern Baja California, and portions of northwestern 
Mexico where Tropical Storm Watches are in effect.
 
2. Damaging wind gusts, especially in areas of higher terrain, are 
forecast to spread farther inland over portions of northwestern 
Mexico and interior portions of the southwestern United States 
today.
 
3. Heavy rains from the post tropical remnants of Rachel will 
continue to spread from the northern Baja Peninsula into Southern 
California, the Great Basin and portions of the southwestern United 
States. This will lead to increasing coverage of rainfall and for 
the potential for significant flash and urban flooding today.
 
4. Waves generated by Rachel, combined with an incoming long-period 
southerly swell, will produce life-threatening surf and rip current 
conditions along the coasts of Southern California and northern Baja 
California. Major coastal flooding has already been occurring in 
some areas, with observed water levels running as much as 1.5 feet 
above predictions. Coastal flooding and erosion are expected to 
worsen this morning as the highest waves associated with Rachel 
coincide with high tides and already elevated water levels. 
Hazardous coastal conditions are expected to continue into early 
next week. Please consult products from your local weather office.
 
 
FORECAST POSITIONS AND MAX WINDS
 
INIT  11/0900Z 32.9N 116.1W   45 KT  50 MPH...POST-TROP/INLAND
 12H  11/1800Z 36.1N 115.3W   35 KT  40 MPH...POST-TROP/INLAND
 24H  12/0600Z...DISSIPATED
 
$$
Forecaster Katz/Blake

item.description:
Issued at 300 AM CST Sun Oct 11 2026 
000
WTPZ35 KNHC 110856
TCPEP5
 
BULLETIN
Hurricane Simon Advisory Number  16
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP202026
300 AM CST Sun Oct 11 2026
 
...EYEWALL OF EXTREMELY DANGEROUS HURRICANE SIMON VERY NEAR THE 
COAST OF WEST-CENTRAL MEXICO...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 300 AM CST...0900 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...18.7N 105.2W
ABOUT 60 MI...100 KM WSW OF MANZANILLO MEXICO
ABOUT 120 MI...195 KM SSE OF CABO CORRIENTES MEXICO
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...155 MPH...250 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...NNW OR 345 DEGREES AT 6 MPH...9 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...930 MB...27.47 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
None.
 
SUMMARY OF WATCHES AND WARNINGS IN EFFECT:
 
A Hurricane Warning is in effect for...
* Punta San Telmo to El Roblito
* Las Islas Marias
 
A Tropical Storm Watch is in effect for...
* East of Punta San Telmo to Lazaro Cardenas
 
A Hurricane Warning means that hurricane conditions are expected
somewhere within the warning area. Preparations to protect life
and property should be rushed to completion.
 
A Tropical Storm Watch means that tropical storm conditions are
possible within the watch area.
 
For storm information specific to your area, please monitor
products issued by your national meteorological service.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 300 AM CST (0900 UTC), the eye of Hurricane Simon was located by 
satellite imagery near latitude 18.7 North, longitude 105.2 West. 
Simon is moving toward the north-northwest near 6 mph (9 km/h), and 
this general motion is expected to continue over the next day or 
two. On the forecast track, Simon is expected to be near or just 
inland over west-central Mexico later today and move very close to 
the coast on Monday.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 155 mph (250 km/h) with higher
gusts.  Simon is a category 4 hurricane on the Saffir-Simpson
Hurricane Wind Scale.  While some slight weakening could occur, 
Simon is still forecast to move near or over the coast of 
west-central Mexico as a major hurricane today. Rapid weakening 
could occur if the core of Simon moves fully onshore.
 
Hurricane-force winds extend outward up to 25 miles (35 km) from the
center and tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 90 miles
(150 km).
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 930 mb (27.47 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
Key messages for Simon can be found in the Tropical Cyclone
Discussion under AWIPS header MIATCDEP5 and WMO header WTPZ45 KNHC.
 
WIND: Hurricane conditions are expected in the southern part of the
Hurricane Warning area beginning soon, with tropical storm
conditions spreading northward today. Tropical storm conditions 
are possible within the Tropical Storm Watch area within the next
several hours.
 
RAINFALL: Simon is expected to produce additional rainfall totals of 
10 to 20 inches over portions of southwestern Mexico, with isolated 
maximum totals of 30 inches possible across portions of Michoacan, 
Colima, and Jalisco through Monday.  This rainfall will produce 
life-threatening flooding and mudslides, especially in areas of 
steep terrain.
 
For a complete depiction of forecast rainfall associated with Simon,
please see the National Weather Service Storm Total Rainfall Graphic
available at hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep5.shtml?rainqpf.
 
STORM SURGE: A dangerous storm surge is expected along the immediate
coast near and to the east of where the center makes landfall. Near
the coast, the surge will be accompanied by large and destructive
waves.
 
SURF:  Swells generated by Simon will affect portions of the coast
of southwestern and west-central Mexico during the next few days.
These swells are likely to cause life-threatening surf and rip
current conditions. Please consult products from your local weather
office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next intermediate advisory at 600 AM CST.
Next complete advisory at 900 AM CST.
 
$$
Forecaster Blake

item.title: Hurricane Simon Forecast Discussion Number 16
item.description:
Issued at 300 AM CST Sun Oct 11 2026 
480 
WTPZ45 KNHC 110859
TCDEP5
 
Hurricane Simon Discussion Number  16
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP202026
300 AM CST Sun Oct 11 2026

The Air Force Reserve Hurricane Hunters provided some valuable 
information on the structure of Simon overnight.  They found 
that the pressure had dropped to 928 mb, with maximum flight-level 
winds of 135 kt within the small inner core.  Similar to the 
afternoon flight, the whole wind field could not be observed. The 
initial intensity is kept at 135 kt for this advisory as a blend of 
the flight-level wind data, assuming a larger undersampling factor 
than normal, with a slight weight on earlier experimental Synthetic 
Aperture Radar (SAR) data, which showed category 5 strength. 

The hurricane has turned north-northwest at about 5 kt.  This 
motion is expected to continue today, bringing the core of the 
hurricane along the coast of southwestern Mexico.  While some of 
the models have shifted more offshore later today, it is simply too 
close to call whether landfall will occur.  Regardless of the exact 
track, dangerous wind, surge, and rainfall effects appear likely 
over portions of west-central Mexico today in the Hurricane Warning 
area.  After today, the model guidance is in poor agreement on what 
happens due to a weak ridge building just north of the cyclone.  
While the new forecast is nudged westward, it is east of the bulk 
of the model guidance, and we are just going to have to wait and 
see how much the high terrain of the Sierra Madre mountains affects 
the hurricane before having any significant forecast confidence.  

Some weakening should start soon due to the hurricane's close 
proximity to land, and recent satellite imagery could be indicative 
of that trend.  However, Simon is still expected to be an extremely 
dangerous hurricane as it passes near southwestern Mexico today.  
The intensity forecast is extremely sensitive to how close Simon 
passes to western Mexico during the next day or so.  With the 
forecast shifting somewhat offshore in a day or two, the weakening 
rate is lowered some from the last advisory.  This is a very low 
confidence forecast because only a small deviation either east or 
west could result in the hurricane rapidly dissipating after 
landfall or keeping more strength offshore.
 
Key Messages:
 
1. Catastrophic wind and life-threatening storm surge impacts are
likely along a portion of the west-central coast of Mexico, and a
Hurricane Warning is in effect from Punta San Telmo to El Roblito.
Preparations to protect life and property should be rushed to
completion.
 
2. Heavy rainfall associated with Simon will impact portions of
southwestern Mexico through this weekend. This rainfall will produce
life-threatening flooding and mudslides, especially in areas of
steep terrain.
 
3. Swells will affect portions of the southwestern and west-central
coast of Mexico over the next few days. These swells are likely to
cause life-threatening surf and rip current conditions. Please
consult products from your local weather office.
 
 
FORECAST POSITIONS AND MAX WINDS

 12H  11/1800Z 19.5N 105.4W  125 KT 145 MPH...NEAR COAST
